chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Accursed! Accursed is the wealth from which zakat has not been paid.

key_terms.مَلْعُونٌ: Accursed, cursed — one who is expelled from God's mercy; the repetition emphasizes the severity
key_terms.يُزَكَّى: To be purified by paying zakat; the passive form indicates the wealth itself carries this obligation

ai.seo_question: What does the Prophet say about wealth from which zakat is not paid?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) transmits a prophetic tradition in which the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) pronounced a double curse upon wealth whose owner fails to pay zakat. The repetition of 'accursed' intensifies the condemnation, signaling the gravity of this omission in Islamic law. This tradition was transmitted to early Shia communities who understood zakat not merely as a religious tax but as a purification of one's wealth that wards off Divine displeasure.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘Accursed! Accursed, is the wealth which has not been purified (by paying Zakāt from it)’.
en.sarwar: 8. Afi ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘ Umayr from abu Ayyub from abu Basir who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah has said, ‘Condemned and condemned indeed is one who refuses to pay zakat.’”
